podcast.title: Co-Writer Confirmation
podcast.body: In 2016, Joel Franks, identified as the co-writer of "Ready and Steady," was located. He possessed another recording of the song, which helped to confirm the identity and partially resolve the long-standing mystery. "In 2016, the co-writer of Ready and Steady, Joel Franks, was found."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mystery Identity Solved
podcast.body: The mystery of DA's identity took decades to solve, finally being cracked when a search through the US Copyright Office revealed a track entitled "Ready and Steady" credited to composer Dennis Armand Lucci and Jim Franks, registered in 1986. Further investigation revealed Dennis was a mortgage broker in California who fronted a part-time local band called DA and the Dukes, and he had died in 2005. "It took decades, but the mystery was finally solved after someone thought to search through the US copyright office."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unexplained Chart Placement
podcast.body: The track, despite being unreleased and without any sales or airplay, managed to nearly crack the Billboard Hot 100. It is believed an unknown record promoter with connections to a major label somehow manipulated its placement on the charts, though the exact method remains unknown. "It appears that an unknown record promoter who had connections with a major label somehow got it on the charts without any sales and without any airplay."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unreleased Billboard Chart Entry
podcast.body: The song "Ready and Steady" by DA was the only song without an official release to ever appear on any Billboard chart in history, reaching number 102 on June 23, 1979. No physical copy was ever found, leading some to question its very existence before the mystery was resolved. "It appears that Ready and Steady by DA was the only song without an official release to appear on any Billboard chart in the history of Billboard charts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
